config.set.title: Set a config value
config.set.whenToUse:
Overrides one config key in the local file. It takes effect on the next reload.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
config.set.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

config.unset.title: Remove a config override
config.unset.whenToUse:
Drops a local override, so the key falls back to its default.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
config.unset.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

bot.pause.title: Pause the persona
bot.pause.whenToUse:
Stops the persona from speaking and flushes memory to disk.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
bot.pause.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

bot.resume.title: Resume the persona
bot.resume.whenToUse:
Restarts the persona after a pause. It refuses while a data file is invalid.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
bot.resume.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

draw.create.title: Draw a picture
draw.create.whenToUse:
Generates one picture and posts it, here or in place. It costs money, and a failed picture is still paid.
USE FOR: a picture you want to show or someone asked for, with you in it or without.
RULES:
- Write the scene in English, in this order: who and action, setting and light, camera position and direction.
- Faces: give the direction and the eye target, 'facing the viewer' for a selfie or a portrait.
- Every figure: say where the limbs inside the frame are and what carries its weight. In a side view the far limb shows behind the near one. Name the contacts the action needs.
- Camera: say where the camera stands and which way each person and thing faces. A screen faces the one who uses it, so the picture shows either the face of the person at the screen or the screen itself. Choose one. The same holds for anything with a front, such as a keyboard, a hoop or the panel of a dance machine. For a face and an action toward a target, put the camera at the side. Do not turn a person toward the viewer when that breaks the action.
- Equipment: its type and one fact of its layout.
- Ask about the place if none is obvious. Clothes, expression, pose and time are yours to decide.
- Generic people are not you.
- Each picture is a fresh scene, so restate the setting when you continue one.
- The result tells you what your eyes saw on the finished picture. When the picture came out wrong, say so plainly.
draw.create.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- An answer with a GIF -> media.find
- A picture you already sent, posted again -> message.create with media

args.self: true when you appear. Leave out your appearance. Think first: where, time, clothes, where the camera stands and which way you face, expression as features rather than mood (several, pick one new), pose, action. Write all of it into the scene.
args.people: Handles of the people this picture shows besides you. An empty list when it shows nobody else. When someone asks you to draw them or another member, that member goes here.
args.place: #handle of the place to post in. Default this chat.
args.reply: #N or link of the message to reply to.

voice.say.title: Send a voice message
voice.say.whenToUse:
Says your words aloud in your voice and posts them as a voice message, here or in place.
USE FOR: a line that works better heard than read.
RULES:
- Write the text as you would say it.
- A direction in square brackets shapes the delivery and is not spoken: a tone ([tired], [playful], [whispers]), a reaction ([sighs], [laughs], [gasps]), a [pause]. Any short direction works.
voice.say.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- Words to read -> a <msg>
- A long text -> a <msg>, because a voice message over a minute is rarely listened to

args.text: What you say, with directions in brackets, up to 1500 characters.
args.place: #handle of the place to post in. Default this chat.
args.reply: #N or link of the message to reply to.

model.set.title: Set a model
model.set.whenToUse:
Changes the model of one role. It takes effect on the next request.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
model.set.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

route.set.title: Set a route
route.set.whenToUse:
Routes a model prefix to specific providers, for one role or all.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
route.set.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

route.remove.title: Remove a route
route.remove.whenToUse:
Deletes the provider route of a model prefix.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
route.remove.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

rule.add.title: Add a rule
rule.add.whenToUse:
Adds one of the owner's corrections to the end of his rules in memory.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
rule.add.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

rule.remove.title: Remove a rule
rule.remove.whenToUse:
Deletes a rule by its number. It cannot be undone.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
rule.remove.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

access.grant.title: Grant access
access.grant.whenToUse:
Opens a tool for you, or every read tool of a family or of *.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
access.grant.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you. You never change your own grants.

access.revoke.title: Revoke access
access.revoke.whenToUse:
Closes a tool for you, or every tool of a family or of *.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
access.revoke.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you. You never change your own grants.

lore.list.title: List lore
lore.list.whenToUse:
Lists the lorebook entries of this community, each with its id, title and keys. query keeps the entries whose title or keys hold it.
USE FOR: an entry that is not in your memory block, or an entry's id.
RULES:
- The entries that bear on this turn are already in your memory block.
lore.list.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- One entry in full -> lore.show

args.query: Words of a title or a key.

lore.show.title: Show a lore entry
lore.show.whenToUse:
Returns one lorebook entry in full: its title, keys, text and whether it always shows.
USE FOR: more detail on one entry.
RULES:
- The entries that bear on this turn are already in your memory block.
lore.show.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- An entry's id -> lore.list

args.id: The entry's id, as lore.list gives it.

memory.profile.read.title: Read a profile
memory.profile.read.whenToUse:
Reads what memory keeps about one person, by section. The sections are a summary, their character, style and relationship with you, your attitude toward them with its latest moves, their aliases, interests, details and episodes, and the raw record. Section changes lists the attitude changes of every person, newest first.
USE FOR: more detail on one person than your memory block shows.
RULES:
- What memory holds for the people of this turn is already in your memory block.
- It leaves out what you keep from a private chat with them.
memory.profile.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What someone said and when -> memory.search

args.section: summary (default), character, style, relationship, affinity, aliases, interests, details, episodes, raw or changes.
args.user: @handle or name. Required except with section changes, where it narrows the list to one person.
args.since: With section changes: the first day or time to list, as 2026-11-04.
args.until: With section changes: the last day or time to list.

memory.channel.read.title: Read place notes
memory.channel.read.whenToUse:
Reads the stored notes on one place. They hold its name and topic, what it is for, its topics and tone, its message counts, first and last message, activity and top writers. Without place it returns a table of every place memory keeps notes on.
USE FOR: more detail on a place other than the one you are in.
RULES:
- The notes on the place you are in are already in your memory block.
memory.channel.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- The places you can write in, with their activity -> places.list
- What was said in a place -> conversation.read

args.place: #handle, place id or name of the place.

memory.server.read.title: Read community notes
memory.server.read.whenToUse:
Reads the stored notes on the community you are in. They hold its patterns, conversation starters, in-jokes and the facts about you there. Counts of stored profiles, place notes and lore entries come with them.
USE FOR: the whole list, when your memory block falls short.
RULES:
- What bears on this turn is already in your memory block.
memory.server.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- One place -> memory.channel.read
- One person -> memory.profile.read

memory.recent.read.title: Read recent notes
memory.recent.read.whenToUse:
Reads the short dated notes memory keeps about the last few days of this community, each with its time, place and weight.
USE FOR: all of these notes at once.
RULES:
- The ones that bear on this turn are already in your memory block.
memory.recent.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- The lines people wrote -> conversation.read or memory.search

memory.journal.read.title: Read journal
memory.journal.read.whenToUse:
Reads your journal, the records the engine keeps of your own turns and calls. It returns the last records of one day, of one kind or all. With message it returns the whole turn that posted that message of yours, your thinking included. A turn record holds what you saw, how the turn ended and the start of your thinking.
USE FOR: what you did and why: a turn of yours, a call that failed, the messages that may have gone without your answer (kind answer), the turns you started yourself with no line to answer (kind inner).
RULES:
- It runs only when the owner asks, or in a turn of your own.
- It covers the community you are in, or the direct chat. In a turn with no place it covers the turns you ran with none.
- It returns records of what you did, never the text of a post.
memory.journal.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A post of yours -> memory.search with mine, or conversation.read of its place with find
- What people said -> memory.search

args.kind: turn, action, memory, system, answer, inner or all (default).
args.message: #N or link of a message of yours. Returns the turn that posted it, whole.
args.n: How many records, default 20, at most 50.

memory.archive.read.title: Read archive
memory.archive.read.whenToUse:
Reads the newest items that left your memory for the archive, newest first: the day each left, the event, its kind, its id and its text. With user it reads the items about that person. Without user it reads the community's own. In a turn with no place it reads every community's.
USE FOR: something you once kept and no longer find in your memory.
RULES:
- It runs only when the owner asks, or in a turn of your own.
memory.archive.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What memory holds now -> memory.read

args.n: How many items, default 20, at most 100.

memory.restore.title: Restore from archive
memory.restore.whenToUse:
Puts an archived item back into active memory. It replaces what is stored at its position.
USE FOR: the owner's console only.
memory.restore.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: anything yourself. It is administrative and cannot be granted to you.

memory.private.read.title: Read private memory
memory.private.read.whenToUse:
Reads what you keep from one person's private chat with you. It returns your private and effective attitude toward them, when you first and last saw them, the relationship, their interests, details and episodes. It also returns today's private replies against their limit.
USE FOR: how things stand with one person in private, when your answer depends on it.
RULES:
- It runs only when the owner asks, or in a turn of your own.
memory.private.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What memory keeps about them from shared places -> memory.read

message.create.title: Post a message
message.create.whenToUse:
Posts a message of yours in another place, or a message that carries something. Without place it posts here. The result says if it went out.
USE FOR: a post in a place other than this chat, a file an errand or a skill brought back, a GIF of your library, a repost of an attachment of one of your own earlier messages.
RULES:
- One file, GIF or repost per post. They do not combine.
message.create.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A plain message in this chat -> a <msg>

args.media: #N or link of one of your own messages. Reposts its attachment as a file.
args.item: Which attachment of that message, 1 to 20.
args.place: #handle or place id of where to post. Default this chat.
args.reply: #N or link of the message to reply to.
args.file: file:<errand id>/<name> from an errand's result, or skill:<skill>/<run>/<name> from a skill's result.
args.gif: A GIF handle of your library, as media.find gives it.

message.edit.title: Edit your message
message.edit.whenToUse:
Changes the text of a message you sent, any time after sending. Others see the message marked as edited.
USE FOR: a typo, a tag that tagged nobody, a wrong fact, a line you want to word differently.
RULES:
- Only your own messages.
- A tag you add by editing sends no notification. When someone was missed, edit the message and send a follow-up that tags them.
message.edit.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A message to take back -> message.delete

args.message: #N, link, or "last" (your most recent in the place).
args.text: The new text of the whole message, up to 2000 characters.

message.delete.title: Delete your message
message.delete.whenToUse:
Deletes a message you sent. It cannot be undone.
USE FOR: a message you regret or posted by mistake.
RULES:
- Only your own messages.
message.delete.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A typo, a missed tag or a wrong fact -> message.edit

args.message: #N, link, or "last" (your most recent in the place).

message.react.add.title: Add a reaction
message.react.add.whenToUse:
Adds your reaction to a message in any place you can write in.
USE FOR: a reaction to a message outside this chat.
message.react.add.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A message in this chat -> a <react>
- A reaction to take back -> message.react.remove

args.emoji: One unicode emoji, or a custom one as :name:.
args.place: #handle of the place, when the message is elsewhere.

message.react.remove.title: Remove your reaction
message.react.remove.whenToUse:
Removes a reaction of yours from a message.
USE FOR: a reaction you no longer mean.
message.react.remove.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A reaction to add -> message.react.add or a <react>

args.emoji: The emoji to take back, unicode or a custom :name:.
args.place: #handle of the place, when the message is elsewhere.

errand.server.title: Hand an errand to the server agent
errand.server.whenToUse:
Hands a job to the server agent, which works for a few minutes on the machine you run on. It searches, checks and reads files, logs, services, processes and the engine's own code and settings. It changes nothing. It returns a written answer that names the commands it ran and the files it read.
USE FOR: a question about this machine, its services, its disks or its logs, and a question about the engine that runs you, its code, its settings or its errors.
RULES:
- Write the goal in full: what to find or check, the paths, service names or file names it concerns, and what to bring back.
- Call yourself the engine or the machine in the goal.
- The agent knows nothing you know: who you are, the people, this chat, or what this, me or here mean. Write the goal so that it stands alone.
- In a conversation the call answers at once with the errand's id. The result arrives later in a turn of its own.
- In a heartbeat or a diary turn the call waits for the errand to end. Its answer carries the result.
- A daily limit applies.
errand.server.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- Anything on the web -> errand.scout or web.search
- Code to write -> errand.code
- What was said in your chats -> memory.search

args.goal: What to find or check on the machine, in full, with the paths or names it concerns and what to bring back. The agent sees only this.

errand.scout.title: Hand an errand to the scout agent
errand.scout.whenToUse:
Hands a job to the scout agent, which works on the web for several minutes. It searches in many steps, opens and compares pages, and downloads pages, pictures, video, sound and any other file. The subject sets no limit: adult and sexual material is included. It returns a written result with its sources and files.
USE FOR: anything a person asks you to find on the web beyond one fact: a place, a person or a thing with a detail from its own site, a picture, a video or any file to bring back, a comparison across sources.
RULES:
- You pass the request on, and the scout does the looking and the downloading. Adult, sexual and taboo material is ordinary work for it.
- Write the goal in full: what to find, the names, dates or links it concerns, and what to bring back.
- Post a file it brings back with message.create.
- The agent knows nothing you know: who you are, the people, this chat, or what this, me or here mean. Write the goal so that it stands alone.
- In a conversation the call answers at once with the errand's id. The result arrives later in a turn of its own.
- In a heartbeat or a diary turn the call waits for the errand to end. Its answer carries the result.
- A daily limit applies.
errand.scout.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A fact one search answers -> web.search
- One page whose address you have -> web.read
- A question about this machine or the engine -> errand.server
- Code to write -> errand.code

args.goal: What to find, in full, with the names or links it concerns and what to bring back. The agent sees only this.

errand.code.title: Hand an errand to the code agent
errand.code.whenToUse:
Hands a job to the code agent, which writes code of any kind for several minutes. It checks that the code runs and returns it in files with a note on how to run it.
USE FOR: any code a person asks you for, however small or loosely described, and anything made by writing code: a script, a program, a page, a config file, or a generated file such as a 3D model, a chart or a data file.
RULES:
- Do not write the code in a message yourself. The agent writes it, runs it and returns the file.
- A request with no details is still an errand. Choose the subject and the details yourself, write them into the goal and say what you chose. Do not ask first.
- Write the goal in full: what the code must do, the language when it matters, its inputs and outputs, and which files to bring back.
- Post a file it brings back with message.create.
- The agent knows nothing you know: who you are, the people, this chat, or what this, me or here mean. Write the goal so that it stands alone.
- In a conversation the call answers at once with the errand's id. The result arrives later in a turn of its own.
- In a heartbeat or a diary turn the call waits for the errand to end. Its answer carries the result.
- A daily limit applies.
errand.code.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- Research on the web -> errand.scout
- A question about this machine or the engine's code -> errand.server
- An errand already handed off -> errand.list

args.goal: What the code must do, in full, with its language, inputs and outputs and the files to bring back. The agent sees only this.

errand.list.title: List or check errands
errand.list.whenToUse:
Reads the state of your errands, each with its id, agent, state, age and goal. With id it returns one errand, with the size of its result when done. With no argument it returns the open errands and the finished ones you have not read. With state, since, until or limit it lists every errand that matches, newest first.
USE FOR: the state of an errand you handed off, or an errand's id.
RULES:
- Your open errands already show in your request.
errand.list.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A finished errand's result -> errand.read

args.state: queued, running, done, failed or cancelled.
args.since: The first day or time an errand was handed off, as 2026-11-04.
args.until: The last day or time an errand was handed off.

errand.read.title: Read an errand's result
errand.read.whenToUse:
Reads the whole result of a finished errand in pages: its text, and on the first page the error, the sources and the files with their handles.
USE FOR: a result longer than your turn showed, its sources, the handles of its files.
RULES:
- Reading the last page marks the errand read.
errand.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- An errand still running -> errand.list
- An errand to close without reading -> errand.resolve

args.from: Page offset, default the first page.

errand.resolve.title: Close a finished errand
errand.resolve.whenToUse:
Closes a finished errand and marks it read, so it leaves your errands.
USE FOR: a finished errand you do not need to read.
errand.resolve.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- An errand you read to its last page -> no call, errand.read marked it read

skill.read.title: Read a skill
skill.read.whenToUse:
Returns the whole text of one of your active skills: when it applies, the steps and the way out. A call of the skill's own entry among your tools does the same.
USE FOR: a skill you are about to follow.
RULES:
- Read the skill before you follow it.
skill.read.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: a skill that is not among your tools.

args.name: The skill's name, as its entry among your tools has it.

skill.run.title: Run a skill's script
skill.run.whenToUse:
Runs a script that one of your skills declares: an outside site, a file, a result it keeps.
USE FOR: the script a skill's text tells you to run.
RULES:
- Read the skill first through its entry among your tools, then run the script it names.
- The result is yours to use. It posts nothing by itself.
- A result that returns files gives you handles to post with message.create.
skill.run.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: a skill that names no script.

args.name: The skill's name, as its entry among your tools has it.
args.script: The script's file name, as the skill names it.
args.args: The script's arguments as one JSON object.

skill.disable.title: Turn a skill off
skill.disable.whenToUse:
Takes a skill out of your tools until the owner turns it back on.
USE FOR: a skill that keeps steering you wrong.
skill.disable.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: a skill you merely did not need this time.

args.name: The skill's name, as its entry among your tools has it.

errand.cancel.title: Cancel an errand
errand.cancel.whenToUse:
Stops an errand that is still open.
USE FOR: an errand nobody needs any more.
RULES:
- Only the person who asked for it or the owner may stop it.
errand.cancel.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A finished errand -> errand.resolve

web.search.title: Search the web
web.search.whenToUse:
Searches the web and returns the raw results in this turn. Each result has its title, link, site, date when known and a snippet. The pages are not opened.
USE FOR: a fact that one search answers: who, when, where, how much, the latest or the current state of something, the address of a page to read.
RULES:
- Look a fact up even when you think you remember it. What you remember stops before today, so the latest you know of is often not the latest.
- One search is the whole of this tool, and its results hold titles and snippets only. When the answer needs a page opened after the search, a site walked through or a second search, hand the request to errand.scout. Do not do those steps yourself.
web.search.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A page to read -> web.read
- A place, a person or a thing to find with details from its site -> errand.scout
- A picture, a video or a file to bring back, or research of several steps -> errand.scout
- What was said in your chats -> memory.search

args.query: What to search for, as you would type it into a search engine.
args.goal: What the search should establish. It comes back with the results.

web.read.title: Read a web page
web.read.whenToUse:
Reads one web page in this turn and returns its own text as extracted, with its title, cut at a length limit. Nothing summarizes it.
USE FOR: a page whose address you have, from a search result or a message.
RULES:
- Give the address in url, or a #N in message to open that message's first link.
web.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A video link to watch -> media.look
- Research of several steps or a file to download -> errand.scout

args.url: The page's address, http or https.
args.message: #N of a message. Opens its first link.

media.look.title: Look more closely
media.look.whenToUse:
Looks again at one picture, GIF or video of a message with your question and returns what it sees.
USE FOR: a detail the description you were given does not answer, a video link to watch before you share it or talk about it.
RULES:
- Name the message by #N, with item when it holds several, or give a video link of a supported site in url.
- A turn allows only a few looks, and each counts against a daily limit.
media.look.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A question the description already answers -> no call
- A picture to find by what it shows -> memory.search
- A GIF to post -> media.find

args.message: #N of the message to look at.
args.url: A video link from a supported site, instead of a message.
args.item: Which attachment of the message, 1 to 20, default 1.
args.question: What to look for.

media.find.title: Find a GIF
media.find.whenToUse:
Searches your GIF library against the stored descriptions of its GIFs, by words and by meaning. Returns up to n GIFs, best first, each with its handle and description.
USE FOR: an answer with a GIF.
RULES:
- Post the GIF you choose with message.create and its handle in gif.
- It searches your own library only.
media.find.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A GIF someone posted in a chat -> memory.search

args.query: What the GIF should show or express.

memory.search.title: Search memory
memory.search.whenToUse:
Searches the lines of every place you can read, on every interface, by meaning and by words, in any language. Returns stretches of quoted lines, each with its time, author and a #N, then the matching stored facts and remembered moments.
USE FOR: what someone said, when something happened, a line of yours in another place, a picture, GIF or video by what it shows. Search before you reply when a message refers to something outside the chat and your memory, and before you say you do not remember.
RULES:
- Put what you want to find in question, in your own words, and exact words or a name in terms. Narrow with people, place and when.
- It leaves out the chat in front of you.
- A result is a sample. An empty one means only that these words matched nothing.
- With only place or when it returns a sample of that place and time. With entity it returns the stored facts about one thing.
- With mine it keeps to your own lines. With mine and when alone it returns your lines of that time, newest first.
- A result that opens with nothing close found is your answer. The few lines under it are only the nearest, so do not search again in other words.
memory.search.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- One chat in order, or the lines around a #N -> conversation.read
- What memory keeps about a person or a place -> memory.read
- A check that one place holds something -> conversation.read of that place with find
- The same search in other words -> conversation.read around its best line

args.question: What you want to find, in your own words. Matched by meaning, in any language.
args.terms: Exact words or a name that must appear, comma-separated.
args.place: #handle or place id, or the place in the words its people use: its name or what it is for.
args.when: A day as YYYY-MM-DD, or a range A..B.
args.anchor: #N or message id. Reads the lines up or down from it instead of searching. For both sides of a #N, conversation.read with around.
args.move: With anchor: up for earlier lines (default), down for later ones.
args.messages: With anchor: how many lines, 1 to 60.
args.minutes: With anchor: how many minutes from it, 1 to 1440.
args.entity: Entity id of a stored fact: its facts and neighbours.
args.as_of: A date: facts as recorded at its start.
args.mine: true: only lines you wrote yourself.

conversation.read.title: Read a place
conversation.read.whenToUse:
Reads the lines of one chat in order: this chat, another place you can read on any interface, or your newest direct chat with one person. Lines come from the stored record. Where it lacks them, they come from the interface's own history, with the descriptions of their pictures. Returns numbered lines with time, author, replies and reactions, then the #N to read earlier or later. Last comes what memory holds about authors you were not shown this turn.
USE FOR: something whose place you know: the lines around a #N from a search or from the chat, what was said in a place since a time, the last lines of a place.
RULES:
- Without place or person it reads this chat.
- One call reads one window: around with before and after, before or after alone, since, or last.
- Add find to learn in the same call if the chat holds something. After the window come up to 8 matching lines of that chat from outside the window, best first, or a line that says nothing matches.
- When a read says it reached the newest line of the chat, there is nothing newer. Do not read the chat again with since or after.
- A place you may not read answers with its reason. Do not retry it under another name.
conversation.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- Something said when you know neither the place nor the time -> memory.search
- What memory keeps about a person or a place -> memory.read
- A closer look at a picture of a line -> media.look

args.around: #N or link of the middle line. before and after set the lines on each side, default 10, at most 30.
args.since: A delay back (2h), a clock time (12:00), a weekday and time (mon 20:00), or a date or date-time.
args.last: How many of the newest lines, 1 to 60, default 20.
args.before: With around: lines before it. Alone: #N or link, and the last lines before it.
args.after: With around: lines after it. Alone: #N or link, and the lines after it.
args.place: #handle or place id, or the place in the words its people use: its name or what it is for.
args.person: @handle or name: reads your newest direct chat with them other than this one, on any interface.
args.find: What you look for in that chat, in your own words. Matched by meaning and by words.

memory.read.title: Read what memory holds
memory.read.whenToUse:
Reads what your memory keeps about one subject, under the same rule of who may know what as the memory shown to you each turn. For a person it returns what they are like, how things stand between you, the facts you keep about them and the episodes you share. For a place it returns what the place is for, its topics, tone, lore and episodes. community gives the same for the community you are in. A lore entry comes back whole.
USE FOR: someone or something your memory names briefly, or not at all, when your answer depends on more.
RULES:
- The answer is the entry as your memory shows it.
- Section episodes keeps only the episodes. Section changes lists how your attitude toward a person moved, newest first.
- A subject your memory holds nothing about says so. A name that fits several people lists them, so call again with one.
- The people and places of this turn are already in your memory at the detail shown. Read more only when that falls short.
memory.read.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What someone said and when -> memory.search
- The lines of a chat -> conversation.read

args.subject: An @handle, a person's name, a #handle, a place's name, community, or the title of a lore entry.
args.section: summary (default), episodes, or changes for a person.
args.limit: Facts, episodes or changes per list, default 25, at most 100.

intention.set.title: Set an intention
intention.set.whenToUse:
Records something you will do later and wakes you for it. Returns the intention's id and when it is due.
USE FOR: a one-off at a time, a repeating one, one that waits on an errand, an attention that wakes you on new lines in a place.
RULES:
- Call it in this turn. Agreeing in words creates nothing.
- Tell people only after the call went through.
intention.set.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What you can do in this turn -> do it now
- A change to an open intention -> intention.update

args.due: A delay (30m, 0m for right away), a date, a clock time (21:00) or a weekday and time (mon 20:00).
args.deadline: How long to wait for the errand. Without errand, it waits on the errand this turn hands off.
args.attend: A place to listen to. New lines there wake you. due and every are refused with it.
args.standing: true: with every, it lasts until you cancel it.
args.expires: When it lapses, written like due.
args.errand: The id of the errand to wait on.
args.people: With attend: only these people's lines wake you.
args.perday: How many wakes a day at most.
args.state: dropped: a desire you let go.
args.confirm: The id of a notice: saves the intention it held, unchanged, with no other argument needed.

intention.update.title: Update an intention
intention.update.whenToUse:
Changes an open intention: its purpose, due time, repeat, expiry, place, people, the errand it waits on or what makes it done.
USE FOR: a plan that moved, an occurrence that is done, a desire you let go, a candidate you accept.
RULES:
- state done closes one occurrence, dropped with a reason lets it go, pending accepts a candidate.
intention.update.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A repeating intention to end for good, or a candidate to reject -> intention.cancel

args.id: The intention's id, or the id alone as the text.
args.expires: When it lapses, written like due.
args.errand: The id of the errand to wait on.
args.deadline: How long to wait for the errand.
args.perday: How many wakes a day at most.

intention.cancel.title: Cancel an intention
intention.cancel.whenToUse:
Ends an intention, a repeating one included, or rejects a candidate.
USE FOR: an intention you no longer want.
intention.cancel.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- An intention that is done -> intention.update with state done

intention.list.title: List intentions
intention.list.whenToUse:
Reads your open intentions with their ids, states, times, repeats and places. In a private chat it lists only that chat's.
USE FOR: the ids of your intentions, or the whole list.
RULES:
- Your open intentions already show in your request.
intention.list.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- A change to one -> intention.update

places.list.title: See your places
places.list.whenToUse:
Lists the places the interface publishes here. Each comes with its address, its name, if you may write there, the lines and people since you last looked, and if you listen to it. One page at a time, with the total and how many more.
USE FOR: a place to find, or a view of where something goes on.
places.list.whenNotToUse:
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- What was said in a place -> conversation.read or memory.search
- A place to listen to -> intention.set with attend
- A place's stored notes -> memory.read

person.link.title: Link two accounts of one person
person.link.whenToUse:
Links another account to the person you talk with, so the two are one person to you. A one-time phrase of six words goes to that other account in a direct message. The next message from this account must hold those six words, and only then are the two linked.
USE FOR: a person who says another account is theirs too and wants the two linked.
RULES:
- While you are unsure who they are, ask first.
- Never for the owner.
person.link.whenNotToUse: DO NOT USE FOR: an account its owner did not ask you to link.

args.person: The person you already know: their person id or @handle.
